summary: ASTRA (Astronaut Status Tracking & Risk Assessment) is a health-monitoring software designed to help astronauts monitor and understand their physical and mental health during long-duration space missions. The system brings together important health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, and mood, in one interactive dashboard. It analyzes measurements, compares them with personal health baselines, and tracks changes over time through dynamic charts and visual alerts. ASTRA also provides simple explanations of health indicators, preventive recommendations, and guidance on when medical attention may be needed. By considering the effects of spaceflight hazards such as radiation, isolation, and altered gravity, the software aims to help astronauts recognize potential health concerns and take appropriate actions. ASTRA supports informed health decisions and helps reduce dependence on continuous communication with medical teams on Earth.

Flame in Freefall: Astronaut Health Monitoring System

Flame in Freefall is an astronaut health-monitoring solution designed to support crew safety during space missions. Astronauts experience physiological changes under microgravity and demanding mission conditions, making continuous health monitoring essential.

How It Works

Our project provides a centralized dashboard for visualizing astronaut physiological data, monitoring vital signs, and identifying potentially abnormal health conditions. It organizes health information into accessible visualizations, allowing users to understand physiological changes and recognize potential risks. The interface serves as the visualization layer of a broader monitoring system incorporating data processing and intelligent analysis.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to improve astronaut health awareness, facilitate early recognition of physiological abnormalities, and support informed health-related decisions. By presenting complex measurements through intuitive visualizations, it reduces the difficulty of interpreting health information and contributes to safer, more sustainable human space exploration.

Technology and Development

The project combines front-end development with data-driven health monitoring concepts. The dashboard is implemented using web technologies, while the broader system is designed to incorporate physiological datasets, analytical algorithms, and health-risk assessment. The front-end repository contains the user interface and visualization components, independently of backend processing.

Creativity and Innovation

Our creativity lies in transforming astronaut physiological monitoring into an accessible, interactive experience rather than presenting isolated numerical measurements. The project connects health-data visualization with intelligent monitoring, creating a foundation for integrating multiple physiological indicators into a unified astronaut health interface.

Design Considerations

We considered usability, clarity, physiological relevance, interpretability, and the importance of presenting health information responsibly. We also considered the unique challenges of space environments, where timely access to meaningful health information can be particularly valuable.

Ultimately, Flame in Freefall seeks to bridge physiological data and actionable understanding, supporting astronaut well-being and advancing safer exploration beyond Earth.
